neighbours.label: a justifying step in a calculus explanation ('this is due to the rule', 'because we know the antiderivative')
fire: The derivative of sin(3x) is 3cos(3x). This is due to the chain rule.
The integral of 1/x is ln|x|, because we know the derivative of ln x is 1/x.
The slope of x squared at 2 is 4. This is due to the power rule.
We can integrate e to the 2x easily, because we know its antiderivative.
The derivative of e^(5x) is 5e^(5x). This follows from the chain rule.
The limit is zero, and this is due to the denominator growing faster.
The derivative of ln(x^2) is 2/x. This is due to the rules for logarithms.
We can undo the derivative here, because we know the antiderivative of cos x.
quiet: The match was cancelled at noon. This is due to the heavy rain.
The shop is closed today, because we know the owner is on holiday.
The derivative of x cubed is three x squared.
We can walk to the park easily, because we know the way.
The integral of a constant is that constant times x.
The road is closed, and this is due to the flooding near the bridge.
The slope of a horizontal line is zero.
We can lend you the ladder, because we know you will return it.

predictions: Fires on the connective that justifies a step in a derivative or integral explanation; quiet on the same connectives outside math and on bare math statements.
notes: Probe: 'This is due to the chain rule' 0.84, 'because we know the antiderivative' 0.48, quotient rule 0.28, 'square of 13 ... so' 0.19; 'due to the storm' 0.02, 'we know the owner' 0.01, variance formula statement 0.06. Sparse pole (0.014%).
